protest-52.claim: Delhi Police registered an FIR against 22 protesters detained at Minto Road on 1 November as they marched from the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan towards Jantar Mantar, Hindustan Times reported on 3 November. Police said members of the Disha Students' Organisation and the Revolutionary Workers' Party of India took out the march at about 5 pm, that Jantar Mantar is no longer a protest site, and that the protesters were taken in two buses to the Dwarka Sector 23 and Jafarpur Kalan police stations and released by 2 am the next day. The FIR is under Sections 223(a), 132, 221, 121(1), 3(5) and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. An artist affiliated with the party was placed in preventive detention at the Connaught Place police station under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita. Before the Special Executive Magistrate at Mandir Marg he refused to sign a peace bond, and he was released after furnishing sureties and a personal bond. A member of the party said the march demanded that Jantar Mantar be reclaimed as a protest site and that the SIR be scrapped. Hindustan Times had reported on 2 November that police said over 50 protesters were briefly detained near Minto Road after the rally, and the later report does not say whether the 22 are among them.

protest-64.claim: The Karnataka Rajya Muslim Okkoota, an umbrella body of Muslim community groups, said in a statement on 9 November that an analysis of the Commission's booth level data by the political research consultancy Sankalp found that 27.59% of the electors in the 10 Assembly constituencies represented by Muslim MLAs were left off the roll, against a state average of 19.45%, The Hindu and The Indian Express reported. The statement calls these names deleted. By the body's estimate, those 10 constituencies held 9,62,359 Muslim electors on the 2025 roll, of whom 2,46,759 (25.64%) were left off, and more than 8.80 lakh Muslim electors were left off in 64 constituencies where Muslims are a large share of the population. By the same estimate, 2,58,770 of the 15,15,088 electors left off as absent across the state, and 1,43,940 of the 7,08,666 left off as already enrolled elsewhere, were Muslims. The Indian Express gives the body's shares as 17.1% and 20.3%, against a Muslim share of 12.9% of the state's population and 12.2% of the electors left off as dead. The body argues that a finding of absent or enrolled elsewhere rests on the judgement of booth level officers and other field officials, where a death can be checked against official records. It gives Chamarajpet 1,07,722 names left off, Kalaburagi North 1,05,257, Narasimharaja 99,367 and Shivajinagar 81,230. It asked the Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission to explain, and demanded that the revision be scrapped, that the previous rolls be used for future elections, that a judicial inquiry be held and that legal action be taken against officials found responsible for irregularities.
